correctedState: CONFIRMED as written, with two clarifications. (a) The idle-drop half of the claim is what `channels.md:13` supports; the grouping half is contracted by `channels-reference.md:256`, not by the quoted page. (b) On a stock install nothing is delivered at all regardless: `getMcpChannelPushEnabled()` (`packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:1149-1155`) defaults to `false`, so the dispatcher is never installed — that default is P10's deliberate security gate and is NOT part of this finding. The finding is about behaviour once the switch is on: with channel push enabled and the source permitted, `SessionManager.ts:2436`'s listener calls `canDeliver()?.redirect(text)`, and `canDeliver()` (`:2399-2405`) returns `undefined` unless BOTH `managed.isProcessing` and `agent.isProcessing?.()` hold. An event arriving between turns is therefore discarded with no queue, no idle wake and no error to the pushing server, and several events arriving during a live turn are each steered in individually rather than grouped. The R3 grouping/idle-wake machinery that cites this exact contract (`deliverMonitorEvent` at `SessionManager.ts:2660`, `flushPendingTaskNotifications` at `:2677`, `task-notification.ts:47-52`) exists and works, but is fed only by `SessionMonitorService`, the cron service and R10 detached-MCP results — never by `pool.subscribeChannel`. The repo's own test `__tests__/mcp-channel-gate.test.ts:90-106` pins the drop, and both `2026-07-26-sandbox-and-managed-policy.md:104-106` and the parity audit `:1167` record it as a known open invariant a later feature is expected to remove — an acknowledged gap, not a settled decision.
